clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: the operative sentence reads "I hereby exempt the said John F. Phillips from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1943". Recorded as 1943-09-30, inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day, under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on until-dates); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption stops when that day begins, is the alternative. Actor: EO 9208 itself, whose registered held text supplies the stated term. The employee named is John F. Phillips.

research_rationale:
EO 9208 (August 1, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt) read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-9208-exemption-john-f-phillips-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, done 2026-11-04: the page record with the same sha256 in the APP mirror records (capture archive common-crawl) has the heading Executive Order 9208—Exemption of John F. Phillips From Compulsory Retirement for Age, date 1942-08-01, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's; the heading names this order's number and its subject agrees with the text. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the clause-drafts copy. The order (read in full, one paragraph of recital and one operative sentence) is a first grant: it recites that the employee will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service and exempts him for one year ending September 30, 1943. First end: the order's own fixed term, recorded as 1943-09-30, inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption stops when that day begins, is the alternative. Authority: section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), cited in the order. No held source shows that section repealed or amended before the stated end; a held later exemption order (EO 9530, March 14, 1945) still cites section 204, which corroborates the authority but is not an event affecting this order.
